university: University of Colorado Denver/Anschutz Medical Campus

documents.unit: Student Conduct and Community Standards, CU Denver
documents.title: GenAI and Academic Integrity
documents.stance_why: The page says students 'assume you DO NOT have permission to use GenAI' unless the faculty member permits it and says 'It is your responsibility to check with your faculty', then offers an 'AI Assessment Scale' of No AI, Plan, Collaborate and Create. It sets no single rule, hands the decision to instructors and gives tiers, so delegates.
documents.summary: Student Conduct's page explains how cheating, plagiarism, fabrication and falsification under Campus Policy 7050 apply to GenAI. It tells students to assume AI is not allowed without faculty permission, gives citation formats and a four-level AI Assessment Scale, and ends with a self-check checklist.

units.why: The page states the Academic Integrity Policy binds every student and sets this page as the application to GenAI; it is an institution-level scope statement, so P56, with 'All students are held to' as the binding language.
units.anchor: All students are held to the University’s Academic Integrity Policy
units.fit_note: Scope statement tying GenAI to existing integrity policy 7050; also touches P77.

units.why: 'we expect ethical use of Generative AI' sets a general expectation for AI use in academic work without banning it; no type for a general ethical-use expectation exists, and P56 is the nearest framework statement.
units.anchor: we expect ethical use of Generative AI (GenAI) in your academic work
units.fit_note: Expectation of 'ethical use' implies AI use is possible; no specific rules in this sentence.

units.why: The definition of cheating covers use of 'devices not authorized by the instructor'; it classifies unauthorized AI-type use as cheating, so P36.
units.anchor: use of information, materials, notes, study aids, or other devices not authorized by the instructor
units.frag_start: involves the possession, communication, or use

units.why: 'Authorization' only counts when given by the responsible faculty member, so the instructor decides what AI use is allowed; P04 as the decision sits with each faculty member.
units.anchor: “Authorization” is legitimate only if given by the faculty member responsible

units.why: Prompting GenAI to complete an assigned task is 'likely cheating'; this bars having AI produce the submitted work (P19), and it is also misconduct classification but the content is the prohibited act.
units.anchor: task, that has been assigned to you by a faculty member, is likely cheating.

units.why: 'your faculty member is unable to evaluate your learning' gives the reason AI doing the work is a problem; it is a rationale about evaluation, closest to P95 (honest evaluation) rather than skill-building P41.
units.anchor: your faculty member is unable to evaluate your learning.
units.fit_note: Reason is that instructors cannot evaluate learning; touches on learning but is about evaluation.

units.why: 'assume you DO NOT have permission to use GenAI' unless expressly permitted gives the fallback rule when permission is silent: P06.
units.anchor: assume you DO NOT have permission to use GenAI
units.frag_start: Like using a calculator during an

units.why: Submitting GenAI work 'without giving this source credit is plagiarism' classifies uncredited AI work as plagiarism (misconduct), so P36; it implies credit is needed, which also relates to P24 but the sentence is a misconduct classification.
units.anchor: Submitting work completed by GenAI without giving this source credit is plagiarism.
units.fit_note: Also implies that crediting AI is required (P24).

units.why: Slightly editing AI output is called 'mosaic plagiarism', closing a loophole by classifying edited AI output as plagiarism; P36 is the nearest type.
units.anchor: Making slights edits and changes to a GenAI output is considered “mosaic plagiarism”.
units.frag_start: Making slights edits and changes to

units.why: Students are told they must find, validate and cite original sources behind AI output; the duty to verify output makes this P31.
units.anchor: responsible to find, ensure they are valid, and cite the original sources as well.
units.frag_start: Most GenAI models are providing information
units.fit_note: Adds a duty to cite the original sources beneath the AI output.

units.why: The page gives MLA and APA citation formats for ChatGPT including prompt text, version, date and URL; this specifies tool, prompt and date, so P25.
units.anchor: “Your prompt text” prompt. ChatGPT, Version, OpenAI, Date accessed, URL.

units.why: The APA format for ChatGPT is a second citation form naming tool, version and date; same type as the MLA format, P25.
units.anchor: OpenAI. (2023) ChatGPT (May 3 version)[Large language model]. URL.

units.why: Factually inaccurate GenAI work 'could be seen as a fabrication', treating unverified AI output as misconduct; P36 classifies it, although it also warns of errors (P31).
units.anchor: factually inaccurate from GenAI could be seen as a fabrication of information.
units.frag_start: Submitting work that is factually inaccurate
units.fit_note: Also says AI output may be inaccurate, so students must check it (P31).

units.why: 'GenAI is known to produce hallucinated sources and results' is a factual warning that AI output is wrong, so P31.
units.anchor: GenAI is known to produce “hallucinated” sources and results.

units.why: Using GenAI to forge documents may violate the Student Code of Conduct: a ban on deceptive AI use under the conduct code, so P74.
units.anchor: GenAI to forge documents may also be a violation of the Student Code of Conduct.

units.why: 'you are responsible to determine the validity of all sources' places responsibility for checking sources on the student, so P31.
units.anchor: you are responsible to determine the validity of all sources that you use
units.frag_start: Remember, you are responsible to determine

units.why: Instructing GenAI to alter or skew results 'may be considered falsification': a ban on AI used to falsify data, P74.
units.anchor: Instructing GenAI to alter, change, or skew results may be considered falsification.

units.why: 'You are responsible to uphold ethical standards' makes the student answerable for ethical conduct; P29 as general responsibility for one's work.
units.anchor: You are responsible to uphold ethical standards while a student.
units.fit_note: Responsibility for ethical standards in general rather than for submitted work specifically.

units.why: The page puts the duty on students to ask each faculty member about AI use in their course, so students must learn each course's rules: P78.
units.anchor: It is your responsibility to check with your faculty about AI use in their course.

units.why: 'this may vary for each assignment' says AI rules differ by assignment, so decision is per assignment: P04.
units.anchor: Be aware this may vary for each assignment.

units.why: The 'AI Assessment Scale' table names four levels of GenAI use (No AI, Plan, Collaborate, Create), a tier system, P05; the four rows are coded as one unit anchored on its first level.
units.anchor: No AI The task is completed independently without any GenAI assistance.
units.policy: The university's AI Assessment Scale names four types of GenAI use: No AI, Plan with AI, Collaborate with AI and Create with AI.

units.why: 'Plan with AI' allows GenAI for brainstorming, outlining or initial research in pre-task work; this permission is about brainstorming (P15).
units.anchor: GenAI may be used for pre-task activities such as brainstorming, outlining, or initial research.
units.fit_note: Also covers outlining and initial research as pre-task activities.

units.why: 'Collaborate with AI' allows GenAI to help complete the task including drafting, feedback and grammar edits; writing support (P91) fits best, though it also covers idea generation.
units.anchor: like idea generation, creating a draft, providing feedback, and grammar edits.
units.fit_note: Level also includes idea generation and creating a draft, broader than editing support.

units.why: 'Create with AI' allows GenAI to complete elements of the task, i.e. AI-produced content as part of the work; P16 (AI-generated content under stated conditions) is nearest though no conditions are given beyond faculty permission.
units.anchor: GenAI is used to complete an elements of the task.
units.fit_note: Describes the level only; no conditions on size or citation, and not specific to code.

units.why: The checklist item says students should confirm faculty permission for the assignment, which repeats that the instructor's permission is required: P78 for checking the rules and getting permission.
units.anchor: I have been permitted, by my faculty member, to use GenAI on this assignment.
units.frag_start: I have been permitted, by my
units.fit_note: Frames permission as a pre-submission check, adding a requirement of actual permission.

units.why: The checklist asks students to confirm they understand how they are permitted to use GenAI on the assignment; this is about knowing the course's rules, P78.
units.anchor: I understand the way in which I am permitted to use GenAI on this assignment.

units.why: 'my own thoughts, words, and tone of voice' says the submitted work must be the student's own, so P29.
units.anchor: I am using my own thoughts, words, and tone of voice.

units.why: The checklist asks students to check sources and cite facts, statistics, quotes to the original author; duty to verify and cite originals: P31.
units.anchor: properly cited any facts, statistics, or quotes to the original author.
units.frag_start: I have checked sources, and properly
units.fit_note: Combines checking sources with citing them to the original author.

units.why: Students should analyze GenAI output to find false, biased and inaccurate information: P31, the verify-output rule.
units.anchor: I have analyzed the GenAI output and identified false, biased, and inaccurate information.
units.frag_start: I have analyzed the GenAI output

units.why: Checklist item that students have 'documented how I used GenAI and have cited it properly'; documentation plus citation, best P24 (disclose with submission) though it also implies keeping documentation.
units.anchor: I have documented how I used GenAI and have cited it properly.
units.frag_start: I have documented how I used
units.fit_note: Also asks for documentation of how AI was used, close to P26.

units.why: 'I have not used confidential, protected, or copyrighted information' bars putting such material into GenAI; the nearest is P49 (not uploading protected works), though it also covers confidential data.
units.anchor: I have not used confidential, protected, or copyrighted information.
units.frag_start: I have not used confidential, protected,
units.fit_note: Also covers confidential data (P50) and copyright (P52); the checklist does not say 'upload'.

units.why: Students should be able to explain all findings and show full understanding without GenAI; this is the explain-every-part rule, P30.
units.anchor: demonstrate full understanding of the assignment without the aid of GenAI.
units.frag_start: I can explain all my findings

units.why: 'I can prove what sources I used and how I verified the information' asks students to keep evidence of sources and verification; the type that fits is P31 (verify), but the proof requirement goes beyond it.
units.anchor: I can prove what sources I used and how I verified the information.
units.fit_note: Adds that students must be able to prove their sources and verification process.

units.why: The closing line says doing the work 'yourself imperfectly' is the truest testament of learning, a learning rationale for doing one's own work: P41.
units.anchor: doing it yourself imperfectly is the truest testament of learning.
units.frag_start: If “perfection is the enemy of progress”
units.fit_note: Frames it as a value statement, not a direct limit on AI.

notes: Single included document. The scale rows are coded as units with the scale-name policy attached to the No AI row. Policy 7050 itself and the TIPS tool page were not coded (not included).
